I am 58, and I have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou all my life. I only went to primary school, but the land is my real teacher. This year I will keep doing what works: I will manage the winter wheat already in the ground on the full 8 mu, harvest it in early June, and immediately plant summer maize on the same land. I will not mess around with vegetables or cotton — prices are unpredictable, and I do not have the extra hands. My son is working in the city, so it is just me and my wife. We need crops we can sell to the grain station no matter what.

For the wheat, I sowed improved seed from the township supply store last October — varieties like Shimai or Liangxing that I know and trust. I rotary-tilled before sowing because our soil is heavy and needs breaking up after the maize stubble. Now that spring is here, I will topdress with urea at green-up; together with the basal compound fertilizer I put down in autumn, that comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times — winter water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I will spray once for weeds, twice for insects, and once for fungus, so four times total. If the weather is normal, I should get around 500 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, after the wheat comes off in June I will plant hybrid seed like Nongda 372 using no-tillage direct seeding. The dealer has a machine that plants through the straw, which saves me time and diesel. I will spread about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, which is roughly 15 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice — once right after sowing to get it up, and once at big flare if the rain does not come. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice, and fungicide only if I see rust, so I figure three pesticide applications. I expect about 550 kg per mu.
